summary: Flushes a mutex-protected singly-linked list on the owning object: waits on the mutex handle (this+0xB2C) with the wait timeout (this+0xB30), then walks every node from the head (this+0xB1C) via each node's next pointer (node+4), freeing the node's data pointer when the byte flag at node+8 is set and freeing every node itself, zeroes the four list-head dwords (this+0xB1C through this+0xB28), and releases the mutex. Called by NetworkCleanup_fbe0 (0057FBE0).

local_names.this: object owning the mutex-protected list (this[711]/this[715]/this[716] dword indices)
local_names.v4: validated list base used for the walk, null when the mutex wait failed
local_names.v5: current node address during the walk
local_names.v6: snapshot of the current node before following its next pointer

operations.description: Mutex acquisition gate: when the mutex handle at this+0xB2C is non-null, WaitForSingleObject is called with the timeout at this+0xB30 and the walk base is accepted when the return is 0 or 128, otherwise the walk base is null
Walks the singly-linked list starting at the head pointer this+0xB1C, advancing through each node's next pointer (node+4) until a null node is reached
For each node, when the byte flag at node+8 is non-zero, FreeWrapper_7bcf is called on the node's data pointer (node+0)
Every node address itself is released through FreeWrapper_7bcf
Clears the four list-head dwords at this+0xB1C, this+0xB20, this+0xB24 and this+0xB28 to zero
When the mutex handle at this+0xB2C is non-zero, ReleaseMutex is called on it
Returns the ReleaseMutex result when the mutex was released, otherwise 0
Invoked by NetworkCleanup_fbe0 (0057FBE0) as part of network session cleanup

clean_pseudocode: base = (handle && WaitForSingleObject(handle, this[0xB30/4]) in {0, 128}) ? this[0xB1C/4] : null;
unresolved: The 128 (0x80) accept-value of WaitForSingleObject is kept verbatim; its Windows wait-constant identity is not asserted here
The node layout (next at +4, flag at +8, data at +0) is evidenced only through the list walk; no node allocation site is visible from this packet
The wait result is treated as boolean success; the distinct semantics of the 0 vs 128 paths are not further separated
